title: Vehicle catalogue registry
description: Shape of contracts/vehicles/vehicle-catalogue.json — the ONE static manufacturer/model catalogue behind the garage's make/model/year selectors. Android, the Cloud Functions backend and the admin web all derive from this single file (Android and the backend via generated mirrors produced by scripts/generate-vehicle-catalogue.mjs, guarded against drift by CI and a unit test), because aggregation ("how many Volvos does the community own?") is only trustworthy if every writer and reader agrees on the same ids. Members SELECT from these values; they never type make/model (Seb product decision 2026-07). The `other` bucket (see otherId) is an implicit extra option that is NOT listed here — it is synthesised at both ends so an unlisted brand/model can still be recorded honestly instead of locking the owner out.

version.description: Catalogue release. Stamped onto every vehicle written with structured ids (vehicles/{id}.catalogueVersion) so aggregation can tell which release a selection came from, and so a later catalogue expansion is auditable. Bump the MINOR part when manufacturers/models are added, the PATCH part for display-name-only fixes, and the MAJOR part only if an id is ever retired (which should not happen — ids are permanent).

otherId.description: The reserved id for the "Other / not listed" bucket, offered as an extra option at BOTH levels: as a manufacturer, and as a model inside every manufacturer. It must never appear as a real manufacturer or model id in `manufacturers`. Selecting it is a SELECTION, not free text, so the no-typing rule holds and aggregation keeps an explicit, honest bucket instead of unparseable prose. A vehicle with modelId === otherId but a real makeId is the actionable signal for growing the catalogue ("someone owns a Volvo whose model we do not list").

minModelYear.description: First year OFFERED by the year selector. Deliberately later than the backend's absolute floor (garage-core MIN_MODEL_YEAR = 1886, first automobile): a bounded, scrollable list is the product requirement, and no Kungsbacka member owns a 19th-century car. Widen this rather than adding a text field if one ever turns up.

maxModelYearOffset.description: How many years past the CURRENT year the selector offers and the backend accepts for a structured write (1 = next model year, so a 2027 car is addable during 2026). Evaluated against the server clock on the backend and the device clock in the client, so a device with a skewed clock can offer a year the backend rejects — that is the safe direction.

manufacturers.description: Every manufacturer offered. Render order is meaningful and is the order stored here: `common` (plausible on Swedish roads) first in rough prevalence order, then the remainder alphabetically by display name.

id.description: PERMANENT machine id, stored in vehicles/{id}.makeId. Derived from the display name once, at authoring time, and frozen from then on: renaming `name` must NEVER change this, or every historical aggregate for that brand silently splits in two.

name.description: Display name. A proper noun — NOT localized, and deliberately absent from contracts/localization/*.json (only the labels AROUND the selectors are translated).

common.description: True for brands commonly seen on Swedish roads. Clients surface these above the alphabetical remainder so the first screenful is useful without searching. Absent means false.

models.description: The manufacturer's models, alphabetical by display name. Trim levels are deliberately NOT separate entries (no `GTI`, no `T5`) — that would multiply the data without helping aggregation; a few culturally distinct performance models (M3, Lancer Evolution, Civic Type R) are the intentional exceptions.

id.description: PERMANENT machine id, stored in vehicles/{id}.modelId. Unique WITHIN the manufacturer only — `3` exists under both Mazda and MG — so a model id is only ever meaningful together with its makeId.
